name: Porokeratosis plantaris palmaris et disseminata
aliases: Disseminated superficial porokeratosis with plantar and palmar involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and histopathological diagnostic criteria for porokeratosis plantaris palmaris et disseminata

criteria.description: Presence of multiple annular, hyperkeratotic plaques with raised keratotic borders on palms, soles, and disseminated over the body
Histopathological identification of cornoid lamella in skin biopsy specimens
Characteristic involvement of plantar and palmar surfaces with disseminated lesions on trunk and extremities
Positive family history of porokeratosis or related keratinization disorders
No evidence of immunosuppression or other underlying systemic disease causing secondary porokeratosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions with histopathological confirmation of cornoid lamella
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on clinical presentation and histopathology; genetic testing is not routinely performed.

common.symptomName: Abnormality of the skin of the palm
Abnormality of the plantar skin of foot
searchTerms: unusual skin on bottom of foot

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing cornoid lamella with dyskeratotic keratinocytes
imaging: Not routinely indicated; imaging may be used to assess suspected malignancy
genetic: No specific gene identified; some familial cases suggest autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic lesion morphology and distribution

distinguishingFeatures: Lesions predominantly on trunk and limbs without plantar/palmar involvement
Lesions arranged in linear distribution along Blaschko lines
Diffuse thickening of palms and soles without annular plaques or cornoid lamella

redFlags: Rapid enlargement or ulceration of lesions suggesting malignant transformation
Secondary bacterial infection of fissured plaques
references: James WD, Berger TG, Elston DM. Andrews' Diseases of the Skin: Clinical Dermatology. 13th ed. Elsevier; 2019.
